text:
Judd Caulfield is a 25-year-old rookie from Grand Forks who spent three full seasons in San Diego before Anaheim called. He's making up for lost time in the most physical way possible: 94 hits in 25 games, along with 12 points, four of them on the power play.

He gets to the net. His 6.49 expected goals work out to 1.07 per 60 minutes, a rate many top-six forwards would envy, and our talent range has his true points pace right around league average. Five goals so far is slightly below what those chances deserve.

The recent ten have been quiet, three points against 5.2 expected, even as his ice time rose by almost three minutes to 16.2 a night. Anaheim has 43.8% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, so his line spends a lot of time defending, which helps explain all those hits. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him close to a typical forward in everything it measures, over only six games. For a fifth-round pick taken by Pittsburgh in 2019, holding a regular NHL job is already a win. Watch whether the power-play time sticks.
